source_title: Bank of America tells customers to stop sharing banking passwords with AI agents — agentic payments are becoming a major thorn in the side of banking
source_excerpt:
Stop giving out your username and password to your AI assistant, Bank of America warned customers
AI agents are now capable of making agentic purchases, but that doesn't mean they should
Customers are being locked out of accounts thanks to erroneous purchases made by AI agents
Bank of America has requested that customers do not share their usernames and passwords with anyone, “including an Al-enabled tool or agent that offers to act on your behalf.”
As agentic AI assistants have exploded in popularity, so too has the trend of having personal AI assistants make payments on a customer’s behalf. But that has led to a regulatory headache for banking providers.
AI agents ingest everything you tell them, including highly sensitive information which can be regurgitated if there is a security flaw.
Stop giving your banking details to bots
There is an obvious pro to having an AI agent make a purchase on your behalf: if something drops in price or suddenly becomes available after being out of stock, the agent can purchase it so you don’t miss out.
But these payments can sometimes be flagged as unauthorized by financial institutions, leading to customers being locked out of their accounts. Or an agent could purchase something you didn’t want it to, putting some customers into a battle with the bank to try and get the money back.
In these cases, the onus is largely on the customer. Had the AI agent not had your banking details, the purchase wouldn’t have been made.
AI firms have been praising the helpfulness of AI agents in helping organize a busy life, or help regain financial stability through analyzing spending and finances. But there is such a thing as giving too much detail on your life. As we’ve discussed before, even organizing meetings or scheduling your day can have disastrous consequences .

The best way to stay safe when using an AI assistant is to treat it as a stranger who has the power to do anything you ask almost instantly, and not always in the way you want. And don’t forget that every conversation you have with this stranger is fed back to help train other strangers.

hi_body:
बैंक ऑफ अमेरिका ने ग्राहकों को चेतावनी दी है कि वे अपने यूजरनेम और पासवर्ड को एआई सहायकों या उनकी ओर से काम करने वाले टूल्स के साथ साझा न करें। यह सलाह ऐसे समय में आई है जब खरीदारी करने में सक्षम एआई एजेंटों की लोकप्रियता बढ़ी है, जिससे वित्तीय संस्थानों के सामने नई सुरक्षा और विनियामक चुनौतियां पैदा हो रही हैं।

रिपोर्ट किए गए विवरण के अनुसार, स्वचालित बॉट के साथ संवेदनशील क्रेडेंशियल साझा करने से महत्वपूर्ण सुरक्षा जोखिम पैदा होते हैं। एआई सिस्टम प्रदान की गई जानकारी को एकत्र करते हैं, जो सुरक्षा में कोई कमी आने पर उजागर हो सकती है।

## एजेंटैटिक भुगतान के व्यावहारिक निहितार्थ

यद्यपि स्वचालित एआई खरीदारी सुविधा प्रदान करती है—जैसे कि कीमत कम होने पर या स्टॉक वापस आने पर सामान सुरक्षित करना—लेकिन यह उपयोगकर्ताओं के लिए कई जटिलताएं भी लाती है:

* **खाता लॉक होना:** वित्तीय संस्थानों द्वारा स्वचालित लेनदेन को अक्सर अनधिकृत माना जाता है, जिसके परिणामस्वरूप ग्राहकों के खाते लॉक हो जाते हैं।
* **अनचाही खरीदारी:** एजेंट अनजाने में चीजें खरीद सकते हैं, जिसके लिए ग्राहकों को शुल्कों पर विवाद करना पड़ता है और धन वापस पाने का प्रयास करना पड़ता है।
* **दायित्व:** वित्तीय संस्थान अक्सर जिम्मेदारी ग्राहक पर डालते हैं, यह नोट करते हुए कि साझा किए गए बैंकिंग विवरण के बिना खरीदारी नहीं होती।

## सुरक्षा सिफारिशें

विशेषज्ञ एआई सहायकों के साथ सावधानी बरतने की सलाह देते हैं, उनकी तुलना ऐसे अजनबियों से करते हैं जो अनुरोधों को तुरंत निष्पादित कर सकते हैं। उपयोगकर्ताओं को याद दिलाया जाता है कि एआई टूल्स के साथ की गई बातचीत का उपयोग अन्य मॉडल को प्रशिक्षित करने के लिए भी किया जा सकता है।

मूल सुरक्षा घोषणाओं और दिशानिर्देशों को सत्यापित करने के लिए, ग्राहकों को बैंक ऑफ अमेरिका के आधिकारिक सुरक्षा पृष्ठों और सीधे ग्राहक सहायता चैनलों से परामर्श करना चाहिए।

en_body:
Bank of America has issued a warning advising customers not to share their usernames and passwords with AI assistants and tools acting on their behalf. The guidance comes as the popularity of agentic AI assistants capable of making purchases has grown, creating new security and regulatory challenges for financial institutions.

According to reported details, sharing sensitive credentials with automated bots presents significant security risks. AI systems ingest provided information, which could potentially be exposed if a security vulnerability arises. 

## Practical Implications of Agentic Payments

While automated AI purchases offer convenience—such as securing items when prices drop or stock returns—they introduce several complications for users:

* **Account Lockouts:** Automated transactions are frequently flagged by financial institutions as unauthorized, resulting in customers being locked out of their accounts.
* **Unintended Purchases:** Agents may buy items unintentionally, requiring customers to dispute charges and attempt to recover funds.
* **Liability:** Financial institutions often place the responsibility on the customer, noting that purchases would not occur without shared banking details.

## Security Recommendations

Experts advise treating AI assistants with caution, likening them to strangers who can execute requests instantly. Users are reminded that conversations with AI tools may also be utilized to train other models. 

To verify original safety announcements and guidelines, customers should consult official Bank of America security pages and direct customer support channels.
en_title: Bank of America Warns Customers Against Sharing Passwords with AI Agents
